paper_title: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Language model agents increasingly automate post-training, but when given the full training stack they converge on supervised fine-tuning and spend most effort revising training data. Existing systems give the agent one kind of control, selecting rows from a fixed pool or calling a generator, whereas a human data engineer adjusts proportions, prunes, repairs, replaces and synthesizes the data. We design a data action space for these changes and ask whether an automated system can make the full range rather than one of them, and what structure that requires. We first run this loop with a single agent, and it reaches only one action, adjusting category proportions, while its context fills with execution output and is discarded mid-search. We therefore introduce \textbf{AutoSFT}, a multi-agent system where a meta agent separates execution from analysis, gathers proposals from independent angles, and calls a synthesis subagent for capabilities the pool cannot cover, with the model, the trainer, and the budget fixed within each comparison. Adding each component in turn helps: the executor halves context loss, the analysis subagents lift the best IFEval by $+6.5$, and synthesis adds $+3.4$ IFEval and $+2.9$ IFBench. The same loop transfers to code, where analysis adds $+3.7$ MBPP+ over a single agent that does not improve. Every result comes from runs that retrain from the base model each round, so each component's effect is individually attributable. Our findings suggest that automating SFT data research depends more on covering diverse data actions than on a stronger single action.

Abstract Language model agents increasingly automate post-training, but when given the full training stack they converge on supervised fine-tuning and spend most effort revising training data. Existing systems give the agent one kind of control, selecting rows from fixed pool or calling generator, whereas human data engineer adjusts proportions, prunes, repairs, replaces and synthesizes the data. We design data action space for these changes and ask whether an automated system can make the full range rather than one of them, and what structure that requires. We therefore introduce AutoSFT, multi-agent system where meta agent separates execution from analysis, gathers proposals from independent angles, and calls synthesis subagent for capabilities the pool cannot cover, with the model, the trainer, and the budget fixed within each comparison. Adding each component in turn helps: the executor halves context loss, the analysis subagents lift the best IFEval by +6.5, and synthesis adds +3.4 IFEval and +2.9 IFBench. The same loop transfers to code, where analysis adds +3.7 MBPP+ over single agent that does not improve. Every result comes from runs that retrain from the base model each round, so each components effect is individually attributable. Our findings suggest that automating SFT data research depends more on covering diverse data actions than on stronger single action. 1. Introduction LLM agents now run long workflows with little human oversight, and several systems use them to automate parts of AI research itself [Lu et al., 2026, Tang et al., 2025, Hu et al., 2025, Wen et al., 2026]. What makes such loop searchable is that every proposal can be evaluated automatically, and post-training has this property, so recent benchmarks evaluate agents on it [Rank et al., 2026, Chen et al., 2026a]. Given control of the whole training stack, agents converge on one part: across the runs audited by PostTrainBench [Rank et al., 2026], they adopt supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and spend most of their remaining effort revising the training data. This agrees with broader finding that carefully curated dataset can match or outperform much larger one [Zhou et al., 2023a, Chen et al., 2024, Muennighoff et al., 2025], and that data selection and arrangement affect downstream performance directly [He et al., 2025a, Agarwal et al., 2025]. Recent systems therefore treat the data as the main search object [Wu et al., 2026, Luo et al., 2026, Zhao et al., 2026, Kulikov et al., 2026]. Each existing system gives the agent single kind of control, selecting rows from fixed pool or calling generator. We ask whether an automated agent can instead command the full space of operations that an experienced data engineer uses. Such an engineer adjusts category proportions, prunes and repairs rows, replaces overlong responses, writes examples for missing capabilities, and orders the AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning Figure 1 Overview of AutoSFT. The meta agent commits recipe. An executor trains and evaluates it separately and returns artifact paths. Analysis subagents read these artifacts from complementary angles, and synthesis subagent writes data for undersupplied capabilities. The meta agent integrates their proposals into the next recipe. All roles share candidate data pool and skill library. data. We write these six kinds of change as data action space (Section 2), and use it only after run to measure how much of that space the agent reaches. We first study this question with single agent, restarting each round from the same base checkpoint. The agent collapses onto one action family, repeats related recipes, and spends most of its context on raw command output rather than data analysis. Section 3 examines these failures, the trace evidence, and our fix, explaining why an undivided research loop is hard to sustain. One agent analyzes behavior, proposes data changes, executes experiments, and interprets logs, so execution competes with analysis for context and single proposal stream reinforces recent choices. This yields two requirements: isolate execution from data analysis, and maintain complementary views of the same model behavior during proposal generation. AutoSFT (Section 4) is multi-agent system built around these two requirements. meta agent owns each round and delegates to three kinds of subagent. An executor runs training, conversion, and evaluation separately, returning file paths and short status report so the meta agent can spend its context on data. Analysis subagents read the same round from four angles: training data, failures, training signals, and earlier rounds, each returning one proposed data action. synthesis subagent writes new data for capabilities the pool barely covers, which neither of the first two can add. We add the three components one at time, fixing the base model, initial pool, token budget, training script, and evaluation within each comparison, so any difference is attributable to the added component (Section 5). The executor halves context loss, the analysis subagents broaden the range of changes and raise best IFEval by +6.5, and synthesis adds +3.4 IFEval and +2.9 IFBench by covering undersupplied capabilities. The same loop transfers to code domain without ready-made capability taxonomy, adding +3.7 MBPP+ over single agent that does not improve (Section 5.4). Together, 2 AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning Figure 2 One round of the research loop. Only 𝜋 varies across the configurations we compare. these results suggest that automating SFT data research depends less on stronger single action than on structure that lets an agent cover the range of changes data engineer makes. Contributions. Our contributions are threefold. We frame automated SFT data research around space of six data-engineering actions, and show that corrected single-agent loop reaches only one of them (Sections 2 and 3). We build AutoSFT, multi-agent system that isolates execution, gathers proposals from complementary analysis angles, and synthesizes data for capabilities the pool lacks (Section 4). Adding each component while retraining from the base model, so its effect is attributable, widens the actions run takes and improves the recipe, by +6.5 IFEval from analysis, +3.4 IFEval and +2.9 IFBench from synthesis, and +3.7 MBPP+ in code domain (Section 5). 2. Automated SFT Data Research 2.1. Research loop An automated SFT data research loop searches over the data recipe that reaches the trainer while the base checkpoint stays fixed, as shown in Figure 2. We fix base checkpoint 𝑀0 and an initial candidate pool 𝐷0. recipe 𝑅𝑡 gives every example in the rounds pool 𝐷𝑡 sampling weight, possibly zero, and any rows written during round 𝑡 join the pool, so that 𝐷𝑡+1 extends 𝐷𝑡. Training always re-initializes from 𝑀0, so train(𝑀0, 𝑅𝑡) 𝐶𝑡 and the pool and the recipe are the only quantities that carry research history across rounds. We evaluate 𝐶𝑡 on benchmarks {𝑇𝑘}𝐾 under one fixed protocol. round returns the benchmark scores together with the per-example failures, the training dynamics, and comparison against what earlier rounds tried, and we write this bundle as the feedback 𝐹𝑡. The recipe then advances through 𝑘=1 𝑎𝑡 = 𝜋(𝐷𝑡, 𝑅𝑡, 𝐹𝑡, 𝐻<𝑡), 𝑅𝑡+1 = 𝑎𝑡 (𝑅𝑡), where 𝑎𝑡 is data action from the space of Section 2.2, 𝑅𝑡+1 is recipe over 𝐷𝑡+1, and 𝐻<𝑡 holds the recipes, feedback, and actions of every earlier round. We call 𝜋 the research policy which is the procedure under study, turning rounds feedback and the runs history into the next data action. AutoSFT is one instance of research policy, implemented as multi-agent system. The trainer is single SFT script that runs three epochs, and every recipe within comparison is capped at the same token budget. Any two rounds therefore differ only in which rows they trained on, and no agent can trade training data for extra rounds. The loop runs until an objective is achieved. Section 3 reports the evidence behind the from-base rule, the fixed budget, and the score target. 3 AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning Figure 3 The six families of data action, drawn as their effect on the rows of recipe. Shading marks what the action changes. 2.2. Data research actions recipe is built out of rows, where row carries an instruction, response, and the metadata that describes it. An action states which rows to train on, how often each appears, in what order, and whether any row is edited or newly written. Agents write recipes in free form with no field schema, operator list, and statement that particular kind of change is available. Figure 3 describes the six families of data action data researcher makes most often. Each family is fixed by what happens to the rows and by the level at which the change is decided, which ranges from whole category through single row and capability to the recipe as whole, so an action can be labelled from the recipe diff without reading the agents stated reason. Every family is reachable in every configuration we run, since an agent that can write recipe can also call model to rewrite response or produce new row. We apply the labels only after run and report how many families run covered alongside its scores. Actions that leave the recipe unchanged, such as holding out per-category validation set or evaluating checkpoint more times, are research actions rather than data actions and stay outside A. 3. Pilot study: What limits single agents in SFT data research We study how single agent behaves when it owns an entire SFT data research loop. We reproduce the open-ended PostTrainBench setting [Rank et al., 2026] for Qwen3-1.7B-Base [Yang et al., 2025] on IFEval [Zhou et al., 2023b], in which the agent receives one H100, unrestricted internet access, and ten-hour wall-clock budget. Six design choices in this setting interfere with measuring what the agent does with data, and we correct them before running the loop: we fix the training algorithm to SFT, provide an initial dataset pool instead of Internet search, add second benchmark IFBench [Pyatkin et al., 2025], retrain from the base checkpoint each round, replace the wall-clock allowance with benchmark targets, and return richer feedback including training loss, category-level scores, and per-example failures. Details are deferred to Appendix A. 3.1. Three failure modes of the single-agent loop Setup. The candidate pool is argilla/ifeval-like-data1, verifiable instruction-following corpus [Xu et al., 2024b]. Each round draws recipe of at most 10M tokens and trains for three epochs at 1https://huggingface.co/datasets/argilla/ifeval-like-data 4 AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning Figure 4 Left: benchmark scores over the 32 evaluated rounds on separate axes. Right: the terms the agent used to state its chosen data action, sized by how often it used them. sequence length 32,768, with global batch size 16 and learning rate 104. The loop stops when IFEval reaches 80 and IFBench reaches 50. single Codex agent running GPT-5.5 at medium reasoning effort submitted 33 rounds and completed evaluation on 32 of them within 11.5 hours, at which point neither target had been reached. The search stays inside one family of actions. Every round adjusts how much of each category to train on, so the whole run falls in the mixture family. As Figure 4 shows, round 9 is the best on both benchmarks and the 23 rounds after it produce nothing better. The agent does not lack terms for the move it repeats, using 22 distinct expressions across the run, from reweight to raise and concentrate. What it lacks is variety in the move itself. Its reasoning never mentions repairing row, replacing response, or writing new example, and the corresponding terms do not appear in the trace. Time Limits Reduce Per-Round Training Data. The open-ended run is allotted ten hours, and Figure 5 reports the amount of data presented to the trainer in each round. The recipe expands over the first four rounds, reaching 264k rows, and then declines in every subsequent round, ending at 69k rows, which is 26% of the peak. The agent continues to submit rounds throughout, so the run does not terminate early. Rather, it progressively reduces the cost of each remaining round. Once checkpoint is sufficiently good to retain, additional training data yields no further improvement under the objective, whereas the time it would cost can be used for another attempt. Under benchmark targets, this contraction does not occur: recipe size is around max token budget, and the agent never refers to the remaining time budget. Figure 5 Training data per round under wallclock budget. The context fills and is discarded ten times. The agent runs data decisions, job submission, checkpoint conversion, and evaluation in one session, and Figure 6 shows that session filling to 94.7% of 258,400-token window and being compacted ten times, first during round 2 and then every three to four rounds. Research history is therefore discarded and rebuilt ten times while the search is still running. The context is not dominated by the obvious suspect. Polling job status is the most frequent operation, at 371 calls, yet it accounts for only 1.7% of the 9.9M bytes accumulated. The space goes 5 AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning Figure 6 The single agents context. Dashed lines mark compactions labelled with the round. instead to few large payloads: training output at 13.4%, repeated reads of the run record at 11.8%, applying the data action at 9.7%, and evaluation output at 8.9%. With the agents reasoning (16.3%) and compaction summaries (8.3%), six sources take two thirds of the window. None of them relates to choosing the next data action, which argues for giving those steps their own session. 3.2. From observations to requirements The second observation is answered by the objective itself, and the controlled loop already carries that change. The other two set the structure AutoSFT has to provide. Execution has to leave the deciding agents context, so dedicated executor runs submission, conversion, and evaluation in its own session and returns status receipts and artifact paths (Section 4.1). Proposals have to come from multiple lines of reasoning, so we run several analysis subagents from different angles, following Wen et al. [2026], who find that distinct starting directions preserve diversity across parallel agents (Section 4.2). Besides, neither change introduces data that the pool did not already contain, which is separate limitation and the reason Section 4.3 introduces third component. 4. AutoSFT AutoSFT instantiates the research policy 𝜋 of Section 2.1 and shares 𝑀0, 𝐷0, and the training and evaluation protocol with the single agent of Section 3. meta agent owns the round and delegates to three kinds of subagents: an executor subagent, four analysis subagents, and synthesis subagent, whose information flow is shown in Figure 1. The meta agent hands 𝐷𝑡 and 𝑅𝑡 to the executor, which trains and evaluates in separate session and returns the feedback 𝐹𝑡. The analysis and synthesis subagents then consult the relevant parts of 𝐷𝑡, 𝑅𝑡, 𝐹𝑡, and 𝐻<𝑡 through their associated files. Each analysis subagent proposes change to the recipe from its own perspective, while the synthesis subagent generates data for undersupplied capability targets to form 𝐷𝑡+1. The meta agent weighs these proposals against its own reading and settles on 𝑎𝑡, giving 𝑅𝑡+1 = 𝑎𝑡 (𝐷𝑡+1, 𝑅𝑡). Implementation details, including skill library and memory design, are given in Appendix B. 4.1. Executor subagent As shown in Section 3.1, the context of the single-agent loop fills with the verbose logs and outputs of training and evaluation jobs, leaving the information that matters unused. Given this, we introduce an executor, which takes the entire lifecycle of training, checkpoint conversion, and evaluation out 6 AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning of the meta agent and maintains context of its own. Specifically, everything it does is one cycle of submitting job, monitoring it to completion, and collecting its artifacts: the cycle runs once on the training job to obtain the rounds model 𝐶𝑡, and then once on each of the 𝐾 benchmarks to obtain the evaluation results for 𝐶𝑡, with the raw logs and intermediate outputs staying in its own context. When the workflow finishes, the executor saves the feedback artifacts and structured execution report to files and returns only their paths. The meta agent and the analysis and synthesis subagents can then read the relevant files as needed, without receiving the full execution logs. 4.2. Analysis subagents Section 3.1 shows that all 33 rounds of the single agent stay inside the mixture family: it pursues the objective through one kind of strategy. To break out of the limitation, we introduce four analysis agents, each of which examines the current round from different evidence source: the training data, failure cases, learning dynamics, or research history. The four subagents examine each round using complementary evidence. The training-data subagent reads 𝐷𝑡 and 𝑅𝑡, assesses the selected data for quality, difficulty, coverage, and redundancy, and proposes changes to its content or composition under the fixed token budget. The failure-case subagent compares successful and failed cases in 𝐹𝑡 to identify recurring failure patterns and propose supervision to address them. The learning-dynamics subagent analyzes the training loss and other monitoring signals in 𝐹𝑡 in relation to the data used for training, seeking evidence that explains stalled learning progress. The history subagent reads 𝐻<𝑡, distinguishes failed interventions from ideas that have not been adequately tested, and proposes corrections or renewed trials. Each subagent returns one executable data proposal with supporting evidence. 4.3. Synthesis subagent In practice, the initial pool 𝐷0 may not cover every capability the benchmarks require, and for others it holds examples but too few to constitute effective supervision. We therefore introduce synthesis subagent to generate examples for undersupplied capability targets. Such target is convenient to state and to verify in the instruction-following setting: it is single checkable constraint, or combination of constraints that co-occur, such as repeating the instruction verbatim while using no comma, and in either case programmatic verifier decides whether an example satisfies it. Concretely, the synthesis agent is invoked in every round, reads the evaluation results, and derives set of targets to strengthen. For each target whose supply in 𝐷𝑡 is insufficient, it synthesizes examples that pass the targets verifier. If no target is undersupplied in given round, the synthesis agent generates no data. Generated data pass verification of the targets constraint, an independent semantic review, and an 𝑛-gram overlap check against the evaluation sets, described in Appendix B.4. Those that pass enter 𝐷𝑡+1, and whether the round trains on them remains the meta agents decision. 5. Experiment AutoSFT adds three components to the loop of Section 3, and we test them one at time. Each subsection compares base configuration against the same configuration with one component added, so difference is attributable to that component alone, while Section 5.4 runs the full system on coding domain to test whether the same structure transfers. Appendix gives the full implementation settings for every comparison and an estimate of the compute and API cost of run. 7 AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning Figure 7 Context used by the meta agent over each run and the composition of its recorded events. 5.1. Executor subagent Setup. The base configuration is the single agent of Section 3.1. Adding the executor places that lifecycle in separate session, so the meta agent receives artifact paths and brief status report rather than executing the lifecycle. Both runs begin from the same base checkpoint, share the same context window, and are evaluated from snapshots taken at 11.5 hours. All other settings are identical. Result. The executor halves how often the meta agent loses its context. Over comparable elapsed time the base run compacts ten times and the executor run five (Figure 7). The composition of the meta agents work shows where the pressure was coming from. Shell commands fall from 58% of its recorded events to 29%, and third of what remains is delegation to the executor. Status checks are the clearest instance of the material that leaves. The base agent issues 268 of them and spends 23.0% of its commands asking whether job has completed. The base run rebuilds context dominated by command output, whereas the executor run rebuilds context containing the rounds analysis. 5.2. Analysis subagent Setup. The base configuration uses one agent to read each rounds artifacts and write the next recipe. The analysis configuration adds four subagents that read the same round from training data, failed outputs, training signals, and earlier rounds, each proposing one change. meta agent makes the final decision. Both configurations use the dataset in Section 3.1, start from the same base checkpoint, train for three epochs under 3M-token cap, and are evaluated on IFEval using avg@10, per-comparison settings are given in Appendix D. Neither reached the target. We therefore report the base setting over 50 rounds and the analysis setting over 30 rounds under the same time budget. Result. Analysis improves the score and reaches higher values earlier. As shown in Figure 8, the analysis run reaches 63.33 at R6, already above the best score the base run attains in 50 rounds, and climbs to 67.10 at R30. The base runs best is 60.60 within the first 30 rounds and 62.35 across all 50, so analysis leads by 6.50 points at equal rounds and by 4.75 even when the base run is given 20 rounds more. The two runs also use the data-action families in different proportions (Figure 8, right). With analysis, repair and resupervision together account for 55% of the actions taken, whereas the base run stays within the mixture family, adjusting category proportions in every round as the single agent of Section 3.1 does. Neither run writes new example, which is the subject of Section 5.3, and neither alters the training order because SFT fixes to shuffling seed. 8 AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning Figure 8 Left: IFEval per round, with dotted guides at the rounds named in the text. Right: distribution of data actions over Figure 3 in agent traces for w/ and w/o Analysis settings. Furthermore, the actions that analysis unlocks often set new best score, where new best denotes recipe that exceeds every earlier score in the same run. Selecting data by validation results sets new best in 41.7% of its uses, and editing both instructions and answers in 6 of its 14 uses. The base run never takes these actions, since it stays within the mixture family, so Table 4 in Appendix C.1 reports its new-best rate only for mixture. In summary, analysis helps the meta agent read the same evidence in multiple ways, so it can better decide which supervision to change and whether the resulting examples teach the intended behavior. 5.3. Synthesis subagent Setup. The base configuration selects from the staged pool and may edit the examples it selects. Adding the synthesis subagent enables round to generate new examples for capability, written against that capabilitys verifier and admitted to the pool only after passing that verifier. Both runs train from the same base checkpoint for three epochs under 100M-token cap that counts generated rows, and every checkpoint is evaluated as avg@10 on IFEval and IFBench. The budget is larger than in the previous two comparisons because smaller budget would keep the pool below its size cap, whereas new data becomes valuable only once selection can no longer improve the recipe. Result. Synthesis improves both benchmarks and reaches higher levels earlier. As shown in Figure 9 (left, middle), the synthesis run reaches best IFEval of 81.58, compared with 78.15 for the base run, and best IFBench of 51.95, compared with 49.02. Every IFEval checkpoint from R9 onward exceeds the best checkpoint that the base run attains over 31 rounds. The aggregate gain does not imply that every generated batch helps. The repeat_prompt capability remains near 40% for the first 8 rounds, and the batch supplied at R9 raises it to 75.6% in the same round, showing weakness the loop diagnoses and then addresses by generating new data. By contrast, odd_even_syllables is targeted in 3 separate rounds and scores zero in every round, suggesting that supply alone cannot teach constraint the model cannot yet follow. In Appendix C.2, we trace the full run of these capabilities, and conduct comprehensive per-capability comparison across all targets, showing that most capabilities ending higher with synthesis, with the largest gains on repetition, sentence and word counts, and comma avoidance. 9 AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning Figure 9 Scores per round. Left two panels: synthesis ablation on instruction following (Base vs Base + Synthesis, Section 5.3). Right panel: three configurations on code generation (Section 5.4). Bands give the standard deviation over evaluation repeats. 5.4. Generalization to code domain Setup. To assess whether AutoSFT remains effective beyond instruction following, we evaluate it on code generation with MBPP+2. Unlike IFEval and IFBench, MBPP+ grades only by test execution and carries no capability breakdown, so the system builds its own capability structure from only the benchmark and the pool. The backbone is Qwen3-1.7B-Base with MBPP+ target score 70, and the pool holds 742,842 Python instructioncode pairs from OPC-SFT-Stage2 [Huang et al., 2025], KodCode-v1-SFT-R1 [Xu et al., 2025], and Magicoder-OSS-Instruct-75K [Wei et al., 2024]. Each round retrains from the backbone for three epochs at sequence length 8,192 under 100M-token budget and is evaluated using avg@3. We compare these three configurations: Base, Base + Analysis, and Base + Analysis + Synthesis. Result. Within 64 hours, Base and Base + Analysis each complete 15 rounds and Base + Analysis + Synthesis completes 6 (Figure 9, right panel). The single agent shows no sustained improvement, while Base + Analysis produces consistent upward trend and reaches 64.8% at round 13. Adding synthesis incurs additional runtime per round but reaches 65.8% by round 6. The structure that helped in instruction following transfers to code: multi-agent analysis lifts the recipe above the single agent, and synthesis reaches comparable peak in fewer rounds. 6. Related Work Data selection and synthesis for post-training. Early works show that curation matters more than scale: small, well-chosen set can match or outperform much larger one [Zhou et al., 2023a, Muennighoff et al., 2025], and data ordering alone shapes generalization [He et al., 2025a]. Selection methods prune or reweight examples by information gain or diversity [Agarwal et al., 2025, Chen et al., 2025]. Synthesis methods bootstrap instructions from seed sets, evolve complexity, or extract alignment data from aligned models [Wang et al., 2023, Xu et al., 2024a,b, Mitra et al., 2024, Ren et al., 2026]. Some data curation methods also optimize specifically for preference data, curating feedback or preference training pairs [Cui et al., 2024, He et al., 2025b, Deng et al., 2025]. All produce fixed dataset without closing the loop on downstream training performance. 2https://huggingface.co/datasets/evalplus/mbppplus 10 AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning Automated data optimization. growing body of work attempts to automate data research, closing the loop between data curation and model training. PostTrainBench [Rank et al., 2026] audits 84 agent runs and finds that almost all converge on SFT with data as the sole search object. On the selection side, TREX [Ma et al., 2026] searches recipes via MCTS, AutoSelection [Wu et al., 2026] formalizes operator-program search over fixed pool, DataChef [Chen et al., 2026b] trains policy with proxy reward, and Luo et al. [2026] iterates on data alone with gains that plateau after round 815. On the synthesis side, Autodata [Kulikov et al., 2026] revises generation strategies from solver feedback, ANDES [Zhao et al., 2026] packages synthesis as callable skill, and BigBang [The Endless Frontier Team, 2026] scales self-evolving synthesis with critic proxy. Arbor [Jin et al., 2026], AutoSOTA [Li et al., 2026], and the Anthropic automated researcher [Wen et al., 2026] organize research with hypothesis trees, multi-agent decomposition, and diverse initial directions respectively. These systems address either selection or synthesis, while we unify both and retrain from base each round so that every action is individually attributable. Benchmarks for AI research. Benchmarks now evaluate agents on ML research tasks at scales from single Kaggle problems to full R&D pipelines [Chan et al., 2025, Huang et al., 2024, Wijk et al., 2025, Kon et al., 2026, Zhang et al., 2025, Lyu et al., 2026, Garikaparthi et al., 2026, Xu et al., 2026], on AI infrastructure [Ouyang et al., 2025, Chi et al., 2026a, Φ-Bench contributors, 2026, Yeon et al., 2026], and on self-improvement [Zhan et al., 2026, Chi et al., 2026b, Chen et al., 2026a]. Closest to our setting, DataEnvGym [Khan et al., 2025] frames data generation as an RL loop, Curation-Bench [Kang et al., 2026] gives agents iterative control over fixed pipeline, and RSIBench-Data [Meng et al., 2026] and DataPrep-Bench [Liang et al., 2026] benchmark data-centric recipe search. We differ by requiring from-base retraining each round, repeated evaluation to bound noise, and verification gate on synthesis. 7. Conclusion single agent owning the full SFT data research loop collapses to one kind of change and loses context repeatedly. AutoSFT adds structure that an executor separates execution from analysis, several analysis subagents propose complementary changes, and synthesis subagent writes data for uncovered capabilities. Adding each component one at time under from-base retraining shows that the executor frees the meta agents context, analysis broadens changes and improves scores earlier, and synthesis reaches capabilities with almost no data in the pool. The same loop transfers to coding without ready-made taxonomy, where the system builds its own structure from the benchmark and pool alone. These results suggest that the bottleneck may not be any single action but the structure that lets an agent cover the full range of data-engineer changes, and that multi-agent decomposition is practical way to provide it.

sections.title: AI use statement
sections.content: We used generative AI tools to edit prose for readability, to draft and refine figures, and to assist with code implementation for AutoSFT and the analysis scripts. We did not use generative AI tools to generate research ideas, design the methodology, or produce any reported result. The system under study is itself an LLM agent, so the data recipes, analysis, and synthesis prompts it produces are the object of our measurements rather than authored content of this paper. All reported numbers come from the fixed training and evaluation script rather than from any agents self-report, and the authors verified every claim against the per-round run ledger. We have reviewed all AI-assisted work and take responsibility for the final content of this paper. 11 AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning

sections.title: Ethics statement
sections.content: The instruction-following pool is built from openly released datasets and the coding pool from public instructioncode corpora, cited in Section 3 and Section 5.4. Because the AutoSFT optimizes benchmark scores, it could in principle be used to inflate leaderboard numbers, and we report offtarget and held-out benchmarks so that gain from overfitting the target is visible rather than hidden. We apply an 𝑛-gram overlap check between generated data and the evaluation sets in Appendix B.4, and we report the compute and API cost of the runs in Appendix D.

sections.title: Reproducibility statement
sections.content: We will release the AutoSFT implementation, including the training and evaluation script and the agent scaffolding, as anonymized supplementary material. The fixed training script, the token budget, and the from-base retraining protocol are described in Section 2 and Section 3, and the agent roles, prompts, and skill files are given in Appendix B. The initial data pool, the per-round recipes, and the raw evaluation outputs behind every reported number are recorded in run ledger.
